dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL or Fujitsu/NEC COBOL on Linux/Unix; uses BINARY-LONG SYNC, COMP-X, RECORD BINARY SEQUENTIAL, and Japanese comments/half-width katakana display strings. Could also be Fujitsu NetCOBOL.

purpose.domain_detail: File I/O test utility that reads a binary sequential input file and writes all 256 byte values (0x00-0xFF) to an output file, with file dump and datetime logging via external subprograms.
purpose.summary: TEST01 opens an input binary sequential file (PIN1-F) and reads through it logging records via a FILEDUMP subprogram. It then writes all 256 possible single-byte values (0x00-0xFF) each followed by CR+LF to an output file (POT1-F). The program is used to test binary sequential file I/O behavior, particularly around special byte values like 0x0D and 0x0A.

notable_features: ORGANIZATION IS RECORD BINARY SEQUENTIAL (non-standard clause)
Japanese comments and half-width katakana in DISPLAY statements
COPY with REPLACING using == == delimiter pattern
REDEFINES used for byte-level access (PIC-Halfword REDEFINES PIC-XX)
verdict.notes: Source contains Japanese text (UTF-8 encoded half-width katakana and full-width hiragana in comments/display). The ORGANIZATION IS RECORD BINARY SEQUENTIAL clause and BINARY-LONG SYNC suggest a Japanese vendor COBOL (Fujitsu NetCOBOL or GnuCOBOL). The file references COBSAM06.POT1 suggesting this is part of a sample/test suite. No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS present.
